Polycrystalline Ni-based superalloys for aerospace and power generation applications are often precipitation hardened to achieve strengthening at elevated temperatures.

High-temperature strength, at temperatures of sometimes up to ∼80% of the homologous melting point under high mechanical workloads, is often achieved via the controlled precipitation of high-temperature stable L12-ordered γ′ (Ni3(Al, Ti)) particles, metastable DO22-ordered γ′′ (Ni3(Nb)) particles or a combination of both
The stacking sequence of such triplets is of particular interest, as the corresponding interfaces created provide significant strengthening
This study focuses on Alloy 718
